metadata.name: Phishing → Credential Theft → Lateral Movement → Ransomware

stage_1_initial_access.description: Attacker sends targeted phishing email with malicious link

implementation.method: Email with credential harvesting form masquerading as O365 login
detection_evasion: Domain typosquatting (o365-verify.com instead of office365.com)
Hosted on compromised third-party domain
SSL certificate purchased to bypass browser warnings

detection_points: Email gateway: Suspicious sender, brand impersonation, link reputation
EDR: Unusual browser process spawning credential manager
SIEM: Comparison with legitimate O365 login failures
prevention: DMARC/SPF/DKIM enforcement (blocks 30% of phishing)
Email sandbox detonation (catches malicious links/attachments)
User training (reduces click rate from 10% to 3%)

stage_2_credential_access.mitre_full: T1598.003: Phishing for Information - Spearphishing Link
stage_2_credential_access.description: User enters credentials on fake login form, attacker captures them

implementation.method: Fake O365 login form that captures username/password
detection_evasion: Form validates credentials against real Azure AD API
Responds with '2FA required' to appear legitimate
Stores MFA device registration cookie

detection_points: Azure AD: Impossible travel (login from phishing domain server + user location)
Email gateway: Unusual device registration from unknown IP
SIEM: Multiple failed login attempts from credential harvester IP
prevention: Hardware 2FA (blocks 99% of credential reuse attacks)
Conditional access rules (block unknown devices)
Passwordless authentication (Windows Hello, FIDO2)
iocs: User credential database (attacker now has: username, password, sometimes MFA bypass)

stage_3_lateral_movement.description: Attacker uses stolen credentials to pivot to internal systems

implementation.method: RDP access from attacker VPS to compromised user's workstation, then to internal servers
detection_evasion: VPN + legitimate IP geolocation spoofing
Connects during business hours to avoid anomaly detection
Uses compromised user's credentials (legitimate auth, hard to detect)
Disables audit logging on compromised system

detection_points: EDR: Unusual process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe from explorer.exe)
Network: RDP connection from public IP to internal systems
SIEM: Failed authentication attempts across multiple systems from same user account
Windows Event Log: Account logon from unusual time/location
prevention: EDR endpoint detection (95% effectiveness if properly tuned)
Network segmentation (blocks access to critical servers)
Disable RDP on user workstations (forces VPN tunnel)
MFA for RDP (blocks credential replay)
iocs: RDP connection attempts from internal network to external servers

stage_4_persistence.description: Attacker creates backdoor to maintain access even after credential change

implementation.method: Creates hidden scheduled task running reverse shell every 30 minutes
detection_evasion: Task name mimics legitimate system task (e.g., 'Windows Update Scheduler')
Runs as SYSTEM account (blends in with legitimate tasks)
Hidden attribute set (tasklist.exe doesn't show it)
Binary obfuscation + encoded PowerShell payload

detection_points: EDR: Unexpected process spawning from svchost.exe context
SIEM: Scheduled task creation event (Event ID 106)
File integrity monitoring: New executable created in System32
Network: Outbound connection to C2 server at regular intervals
prevention: Application whitelisting (99% effective at blocking unauthorized binaries)
Scheduled task monitoring + alerting
Disable command-line tools (PowerShell, cmd.exe) unless necessary
Process injection detection (monitor for unsigned parent/child processes)

stage_5_defense_evasion.mitre_full: T1070.001: Indicator Removal - Clear Windows Event Logs
stage_5_defense_evasion.description: Attacker clears logs to hide evidence of compromise

implementation.method: Clear Security, System, and Application event logs
detection_evasion: Uses wevtutil or PowerShell to clear logs without triggering security audit
Clears log clearing events if log size permits
Attempts credential stuffing to access logging infrastructure

detection_points: SIEM: Alert on event log clearing (Event ID 1102 - Log was cleared)
Windows Event Log: Gap in event sequence (timestamps jump forward)
EDR: Unusual process calling Event Log API functions
Centralized logging: If logs copied before clearing, gap would be obvious
prevention: Centralized log collection (CUT OFF before local clearing)
Immutable logging (cloud-based, offline backup)
File integrity monitoring on event log files
Alert on Log Clear events with automatic incident escalation

stage_6_impact_ransomware.description: Attacker deploys ransomware to encrypt files and demand payment

implementation.method: Download and execute Conti/LockBit-variant ransomware binary
detection_evasion: Binary disguised as legitimate software update (teams-update.exe)
Uses Windows Crypto API (legitimate function, hard to detect)
Distributed from internal network share (appears legitimate)
Targets network shares after establishing persistence

detection_points: EDR: Mass file encryption process (thousands of files in seconds)
SIEM: Rapid file modification events from unexpected process
Network: Large data exfiltration before encryption (data theft stage)
File integrity monitoring: Bulk file extension changes (.docx → .conti)
prevention: Offline backups (blocks ransomware impact, enables recovery)
EDR with behavior-based ransomware detection (95% effective)
Network segmentation (contains ransomware to initial segment)
Disable SMB v1 (blocks worm-like propagation)
Remove admin rights (blocks process-level encryption)

critical_detection_gaps.gap: Credential theft not detected for 4-6 hours
critical_detection_gaps.impact: Attacker can pivot to other systems before alert
critical_detection_gaps.fix: Impossible travel detection on Azure AD logins

critical_detection_gaps.gap: RDP lateral movement blends in with normal traffic
critical_detection_gaps.fix: Baseline RDP source IPs per user account

critical_detection_gaps.gap: Persistence task created but not monitored
critical_detection_gaps.impact: Access maintained even after credential rotation

incident_response_drill_objectives: Detect phishing email before user clicks (Email security effectiveness)
Detect credential harvesting form (Email gateway detection)
Alert on impossible travel login (Azure AD conditional access)
Detect scheduled task creation (EDR/SIEM response time)
